item.title: Speculative Application
item.description: The European Council on Foreign Relations (ECFR) is an award-winning international think-tank that aims to conduct cutting-edge independent research on European foreign and security policy and to provide a safe meeting space for decision-makers, activists and influencers to share ideas. We build coalitions for change at the European level and promote informed debate about Europe’s role in the world. In 2007, ECFR’s founders set about creating a pan-European institution that could combine establishment credibility with intellectual insurgency. Today, ECFR remains uniquely placed to continue providing a pan-European perspective on some of the biggest strategic challenges and choices Europeans need to confront, with a network of offices in seven European capitals, over 90 staff from more than 25 different countries and a team of associated researchers in the EU 27 member states. For more information check our website: ecfr.eu

item.title: PPCA Secretariat Coordinator, London
item.description: PPCA Secretariat Coordinator, Powering Past Coal Alliance (PPCA), London This London-based role will support delivery of the PPCA Secretariat by coordinating events, steering committee and member engagement, and internal processes ensuring smooth day-to-day operations across the PPCA. Background The Powering Past Coal Alliance (PPCA) is a coalition of over 180 members working to advance the transition from unabated coal power generation to clean energy. Founded in 2017 by the United Kingdom and Canada its membership now includes almost a third of the world’s countries, financial institutions, sub-national governments in the most coal-dependent regions in the world and leading utilities. The PPCA Secretariat is hosted by E3G, an independent climate change think tank, which provides management and administrative support to the Secretariat, plus strategic analysis and advice. E3G is the world lead strategist think tank on the political economy of climate change with a global outlook. We work on the frontier of the climate landscape tackling the barriers and advancing the solutions to a safe climate for all. We translate climate politics, economics and policies into action. We pride ourselves on bringing independence to an extremely polarised discussion and holding policy makers to account on their promises. E3G is consistently ranked as one of the top-ten most influential environmental think tanks in the world by the University of Pennsylvania’s Global Go To Think Tank Index. E3G is dedicated to fostering an engaging work environment with a competitive remuneration package in the non-profit sector. E3G offers a dynamic and fast paced working environment that will value your insight and initiative wherever you are in the organisation. We take pride in our team's commitment, supportiveness, and friendliness. We invest in our staff, offer flexible working conditions and pride ourselves on being an open and collaborative workplace. Role Overview The PPCA Secretariat Coordinator plays a central role in supporting the effective delivery of the Powering Past Coal Alliance (PPCA) Secretariat’s work. The role coordinates events, member engagement, governance meetings and operational processes, ensuring smooth collaboration across a global network of governments, businesses and civil society partners. Working closely with the Secretariat Manager, Head of Secretariat and wider E3G teams, the Coordinator provides high-quality logistical, administrative and stakeholder support that enables the PPCA to advance its international mission and deliver impact across a fast-paced and dynamic policy environment. Key Responsibilities Lead preparation for key events Coordinate logistical preparation and delivery of PPCA events, including agendas, timelines, invitations and supporting materials. Manage event logistics such as venue liaison, travel arrangements and scheduling. Maintain and update the PPCA contact database, calendar and forward plan of key meetings and milestones. Conduct background research to support preparation of meetings, briefings and deliverables. Organise meetings and delegations with senior stakeholders Support coordination of meetings and delegations involving senior political, civil society and media stakeholders. Manage logistics including scheduling, travel coordination, agendas and briefing materials. Support the Head of Secretariat with meeting scheduling. Membership coordination Coordinate communication and engagement with PPCA members. Organise PPCA governance and member meetings, including PPCA Steering Committee, Implementation Committee and Members Meetings. Maintain accurate records of member contacts, engagement and correspondence. Work with the communications team and Secretariat Manager to coordinate progress updates on PPCA work. Operations and Internal Coordination Support the development of effective ways of working and communication for a growing Secretariat team based across multiple time zones. Support recruitment processes, including coordinating applications, interviews and candidate correspondence. Strengthen cross-team coordination by contributing to the development and maintenance of internal tools and processes that support events and Secretariat activities. Support drafting of internal documents, reports and correspondence as required. Provide updates on PPCA activities to E3G internal communications, ensuring PPCA updates are shared at staff forums and newsletters. Provide flexible administrative and coordination support to the Secretariat Manager as required. About You Motivated by E3G’s mission and keen to gain hands-on experience in policy-oriented research and stakeholder engagement in an international setting. Several years’ relevant professional experience and track record in a relevant setting. High level of initiative and be positive, organised, resilient, and able to deliver high-quality work on time. Skills & Experience Experience of events management. Experience of building relationships and networks, and working with partner organisations, coalitions, and networks including senior stakeholders. Experience of project and budget management. Prince 2 or other project management training or qualification would be considered relevant but not essential. Very strong written communication skills and advanced written and spoken English. What We Offer Permanent, full-time position. Work-life balance. Enjoy a 35-hour workweek with a hybrid work model and flexitime. 25 vacation days + additional leave between Christmas and New Year. Pension contribution plan E3G offers a reward and benefits package which compares well with other organisations within our sector. The indicative salary range in the UK for this position is between £41,498 - £44,000, dependent on experience and qualifications of the chosen candidate. Yearly process for remuneration review. E3G will require candidates to demonstrate that they have the right to live and work in the jurisdiction in which E3G employs them. Occasional international travel may be required from time to time. We are unable to provide any relocation assistance to candidates who would need to move in order to take up this position. Your Application Please email your application in English and include: A CV of maximum two pages A cover letter of maximum one page outlining why you are applying for this role and when you would be able to start. Recruitment Process First online interview with HR and Team Members Final interview with HR, Secretariat Manager, Head of the PPCA Secretariat The deadline for applications is July 31, 2026. Whilst we very much appreciate the time you will have taken with your application, unfortunately due to the level of response we receive we will not be able to reply to every candidate. Therefore, if you have not heard from us within 2 weeks of the closing date, please assume that on this occasion you have been unsuccessful. E3G values diversity and welcomes applications from all suitably qualified candidates regardless of age, gender, race, disability, sexual orientation, religion or ethnic background. We aim to build an inclusive workforce that is reflective of the populations we support, and actively seek applications from those who are marginalized and underrepresented. We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations to applicants with disabilities.

item.title: Senior Communications Officer
item.description: Senior Communications Officer, PPCA, Singapore This post based in Singapore, to lead the PPCA’s communications work to enhance the public debate on the benefits and feasibility of the coal-to-clean transition in Southeast Asia and contribute to PPCA’s wider comms activities, reporting to the Communications Lead. Who We Are The Powering Past Coal Alliance (PPCA) is a coalition of over 180 members working to advance the transition from unabated coal power generation to clean energy. Founded in 2017 by the United Kingdom and Canada its membership now includes almost a third of the world’s countries, financial institutions, sub-national governments in the most coal-dependent regions in the world and leading utilities. The PPCA Secretariat is hosted by E3G, an independent climate change think tank, which provides management and administrative support to the Secretariat, plus strategic analysis and advice. E3G is the world lead strategist think tank on the political economy of climate change with a global outlook. We work on the frontier of the climate landscape tackling the barriers and advancing the solutions to a safe climate for all. We translate climate politics, economics and policies into action. We pride ourselves on bringing independence to an extremely polarised discussion and holding policy makers to account on their promises. E3G is consistently ranked as one of the top-ten most influential environmental think tanks in the world by the University of Pennsylvania’s Global Go To Think Tank Index. E3G is dedicated to fostering an engaging work environment with a competitive remuneration package in the non-profit sector. E3G offers a dynamic and fast paced working environment that will value your insight and initiative wherever you are in the organisation. We take pride in our team's commitment, supportiveness, and friendliness. We invest in our staff, offer flexible working conditions and pride ourselves on being an open and collaborative workplace. Role Overview Lead the PPCA’s communications work to enhance the public debate on the benefits and feasibility of the coal-to-clean transition in Southeast Asia and contribute to PPCA’s wider comms activities, reporting to the Communications Lead. Key Responsibilities Communication Strategy : Work with the PPCA Comms Team, the broader PPCA team, and with relevant governments (PPCA co-chairs: the UK and Canada; CTC co-chairs: France and Indonesia) to lead, develop and deliver comprehensive communication strategies that effectively communicate PPCA’s value proposition to our key target audience, closely following the political and media debates in Southeast Asia to identify where strategic communications can be usefully deployed in order to speed up the coal-to-clean transition. Messaging : Develop and refine compelling and impactful narratives that effectively address local priorities, concerns, and opportunities while creating a compelling vision of a prosperous, resilient future powered by clean energy. Identify regional proof-points and case studies, as well as leverage closed-door PPCA engagements to generate exclusive insights. Operationalise narratives with a wide range of communications material (e.g., press releases, press briefings, social media content, op-eds, blogs, communication support during events), ensuring consistency across all communication channels. Media Relations : Bring a strong understanding of the media landscape in Southeast Asia to the PPCA Team. Cultivate strategic media partnerships through consistent engagement, positioning PPCA and its spokespeople as a valued resource for regional energy transition insights. Proactively identify opportunities to engage the media and pitch stories, deliver media assets, develop speaking points and other supportive material for interviews. Stakeholder Engagement and Events : Establish new partnerships and leverage existing ones to refine and amplify messages and identify and elevate local influential voices in comms activities. Use social media to increase visibility and create and strengthen connections. Coordinate online or in-person events for the PPCA Team, co-creating the initial concept and seeing them through to completion. Support the PPCA team in representing the organisation at other relevant events to establish relationships and enhance the Alliance’s profile. Monitoring and Evaluation : Track and analyse the impact of PPCA’s communications efforts in Southeast Asia, including media coverage, social media tracking and stakeholder feedback. Provide regular reports to senior staff and funders on the effectiveness of communication strategies and identify areas for improvement. Contribute to the broader comms activities of the PPCA’s comms team as required. About You A strong track record of building and maintaining impactful media relations in Southeast Asia, including pitching stories and securing media coverage. An enthusiasm to embrace complex, technical topics, and transform them into compelling narratives about the benefits and feasibility of the energy transition. The versatile and adaptable skills necessary to flourish in a fast-paced and wide-ranging work environment and work across time zones. Capability to meet deadlines independently in fast-paced environments. Fluency in written and spoken English, our working language; additional languages are an asset. Skills & Experience At least five years of professional experience in leading external communications, including developing and implementing communication strategies. Proven experience in working in networks with a strong track record of leading on stakeholder management. Demonstrated ability to work with a diverse range of stakeholders, including governments, think tanks and financial institutions. Proven experience in delivering events. Understanding of digital comms tools and platforms, including social media management, website content management systems, and email marketing. What We Offer Permanent, full-time position. Work-life balance. Enjoy a 35-hour workweek with a hybrid work model and flexitime. 25 vacation days + additional leave between Christmas and New Year. Pension contribution plan (can vary according to location). E3G offers a reward and benefits package which compares well with other organisations within our sector. The indicative salary range in the Singapore is $72,000 SGD - $76,800 SGD dependent on experience and qualifications of the chosen candidate. Yearly process for remuneration review. E3G will require candidates to demonstrate that they have the right to live and work in the jurisdiction in which E3G employs them. Occasional international travel may be required from time to time. We are unable to provide any relocation assistance to candidates who would need to move in order to take up this position. Your Application Are you ready to embark on an exhilarating journey where your ambition meets passion? Submit your application in English with a CV of maximum 2 pages and an offer letter of no more than 1 page outlining why you are applying for this role and when you would be able to start. Please combine into a one document submission. Recruitment Process First online interview with HR and Team Members Final online interview with HR, PPCA Communications Lead, and Head of Secretariat The deadline for applications is 31 July 2026. Whilst we very much appreciate the time you will have taken with your application, unfortunately due to the level of response we receive we will not be able to reply to every candidate. Therefore, if you have not heard from us within 2 weeks of the closing date, please assume that on this occasion you have been unsuccessful. item.title: Senior Policy Advisor, Trade Diplomacy, Japan
item.description: Senior Policy Advisor, Trade Diplomacy, Japan E3G is looking for a Senior Policy Advisor to lead analysis and engagement on trade diplomacy within its Japan programme. The new role will sit within E3G’s Global Clean Power Diplomacy team and will work closely with our Japan and trade experts to develop E3G’s work on the intersection of Japan’s trade policy, energy and economic security strategies, and climate objectives – with trade playing a key role as a diplomatic lever across these areas contributing to accelerating the clean energy transition. The role The role will build on existing work on trade and its use as a diplomatic lever, leading the development of strategies and engagements to align Japan’s trade, and economic policies, with the goals of a clean energy transition and ambitious climate action. The candidate will be based in Japan and will be required to work remotely. We are looking for an intellectually curious, enthusiastic person with experience of condensing and communicating complex information into clear, targeted analysis and advice for varied stakeholders. You will be motivated by building relationships with external stakeholders, and by creating impactful outcomes through strategic collaborations. You will have the opportunity to develop the strategy and shape the work programme, in consultation with colleagues in the Japan team and across E3G’s wider trade and industry related teams. Background E3G is an independent climate change think tank with a global outlook. We are world leading strategists on the political economy of climate change, dedicated to achieving a safe climate for all. We work on the frontier of the climate landscape tackling the barriers and advancing the solutions to a safe climate. Our goal is to translate climate politics, economics and policies into action. E3G is consistently ranked as one of the top ten most influential environmental think tanks in the world by the University of Pennsylvania’s Global Go To Think Tank Index. Delivering a rapid, managed transition of the global power system from coal-to-clean, not via gas, is a fundamental condition to achieving the goals of the Paris Agreement. E3G’s Global Clean Power Diplomacy team mobilises diplomatic actors to drive real-world, real-economy progress on ending the global use of the coal power and transitioning to clean energy. E3G identifies opportunities for influence and interventions, collaborates with civil society campaigns and partners, and fosters international diplomatic alliances to create a world where no new coal is built, and where existing coal is replaced by clean, affordable energy to enable a climate-safe world. Key Responsibilities Provide strategic insight and thought leadership on trade and diplomatic engagement with Japan in the context of broader global climate and energy goals. Monitor and track developments relating to Japan’s trade relationships with a focus on key partner countries, including various bilateral and multilateral frameworks and agreements (e.g. FTAs), government strategies and publications (e.g. Green Transformation Strategy; and industrial policy priorities, such as the 17 Strategic Fields under Japan’s growth strategy etc.), as well as commercial drivers relating to both traditional and clean energy supply chains, in order to assess their impact on Japan’s energy and economic security priorities and identify opportunities for strategic interventions. Produce analysis, presentations, briefings and other materials, both internally to contribute to E3Gs strategic thinking, and to a wide range of external contacts to communicate our analysis and recommendations, in both written and spoken formats. Expand E3G’s relationships and networks to relevant institutions and stakeholders in trade, energy and economic security – particularly civil society organisations (CSOs), alongside government officials, research institutions, trade associations and key private sector actors, primarily in Japan and key trade partner countries, to develop productive collaborations that support achieving the programme’s objectives. In collaboration with E3G’s Japan experts and trusted partners, maintain and widen the team’s relationships with diplomats and foreign missions and trade representatives to distribute analysis and strategic advice, for example through organising and presenting in online and in-person briefings. Represent E3G externally through active participation in civil society meetings, as well as relevant conferences and other events in Japan and internationally as needed; and maintain relations to media and provide commentary and insights about their area of expertise when needed. Experience and Skills A graduate degree in a relevant discipline, such as trade policy, international relations, climate and energy policy, development, geography, or politics. A minimum of six years of relevant professional experience in a related field, such as trade, policy, research or advocacy within a government or international organisation, commercial sector, think tank, civil society or research institute. Established connections to organisations and individuals relevant for the role, e.g. government and ministries, trade associations or related research institutions, and the ability to leverage these relationships effectively and in alignment with organisational priorities. Strong analytical and strategic thinking, with an aptitude for learning new areas and consider complex information to make evidence-based recommendations. Excellent communication skills, able to convey information and arguments to others in a clear, accessible and convincing way including in sensitive or challenging stakeholder contexts. Highly organised and attention to detail, able to be proactive and deliver high-quality outputs in a timely manner. Strong interpersonal skills, with ability to form high-trust relationships with various external stakeholders and handle sensitive information with discretion, as well as patience and resilience in long-term engagement processes. Excellent written and spoken Japanese and English. Ability to work effectively and collaboratively in an international team environment. What we offer Initial contract of one year, with possibility of extension, for a full-time position. Fully remote and flexible working arrangements. 16 vacation days + additional leave between Christmas and New Year. Eligible for social (employee health) insurance and employment insurance. E3G offers a competitive salary and reward package which compares well with other organisations within our sector, reflecting experience and qualifications of the chosen candidate. The salary shall be subject to withholdings for taxes and social and labor insurances in Japan mentioned above in which the Senior Policy Advisor will be enrolled. Yearly process for remuneration review. E3G is unable to provide relocation assistance to candidates who would need to change locations in order to take up this position. E3G will require candidates to demonstrate that they the right to live and work in Japan. How to apply Please submit your application in English. Please include: A CV of maximum two pages A cover letter of no more than one page outlining why you are applying for this role and when you would be able to start. Please include a written description of your residency status and right to work in Japan (for example, your visa status, if applicable), in the letter. The deadline for applications is Midnight, Sunday 16th August. Whilst we very much appreciate the time you will have taken with your application, unfortunately due to the level of response we receive we may not be able to reply to every candidate. Therefore, if you have not heard from us with 2 weeks of the closing date, please assume that on this occasion you have been unsuccessful. E3G values diversity and welcomes applications from all suitably qualified candidates regardless of age, gender, race, disability, sexual orientation, religion or ethnic background. We aim to build an inclusive workforce that is reflective of the populations we support, and actively seek applications from those who are marginalized and underrepresented. We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations to applicants with disabilities.

Role Summary Our client is seeking a Policy & Delivery Expert to support the design, coordination, and implementation of strategic energy sector initiatives. The role will focus on strengthening policy development, supporting programme delivery, and facilitating collaboration across government institutions, development partners, and private sector stakeholders. Role and Responsibilities Support development and implementation of strategic policy and programme initiatives. Contribute to programme planning, implementation frameworks, and delivery approaches. Support stakeholder engagement and coordination across multiple institutions. Produce technical analyses, recommendations, and briefing materials. Support programme monitoring, reporting, and performance management. Contribute to institutional strengthening and knowledge-sharing initiatives. Requirements Experience Required Minimum 8 years of experience in policy, advisory, reform, or delivery roles. Experience working with government institutions and development partners. Demonstrated policy drafting and implementation experience. Technical Requirements Advanced degree in Public Policy, Economics, Development Studies, Energy Policy, Law, or related field. Strong understanding of policy development and programme implementation. Experience supporting strategic planning and delivery processes Other Skills Strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities. Excellent written and verbal communication skills. Effective stakeholder engagement capability. Working Arrangement Based full-time in Lilongwe, with periodic travel within Malawi as required. Terms of Agreement Start Date: To be confirmed Contracting Period: 12 months Important Notice This exercise is intended to identify and establish a pool of qualified candidates for this potential future opportunity. Participation does not constitute an offer of employment or guarantee appointment to any position. Closing Date: 2026-06-30

item.title: Senior Analyst - China & Asia Pacific
item.description: We don’t just talk, we do. Lead the change with us. At the Tony Blair Institute for Global Change, we work with political leaders around the world to drive change. We help governments turn bold ideas into reality so they can deliver for their people. We do it by advising on strategy, policy and delivery, unlocking the power of technology across all three. And by sharing what we learn on the ground, so everyone can benefit. We do it to build more open, inclusive and prosperous countries for people everywhere. We are a global team of over 800 changemakers, operating in more than 40 countries, across five continents. We are political strategists, policy experts, delivery practitioners, technology specialists and more. We speak more than 45 languages. We are working on over 100 projects, tackling some of the world’s biggest challenges. We’re all here at TBI to make a difference. In a world of ever more complex challenges, we believe diversity of background and perspective is a strength. We pride ourselves on a culture that values and nurtures difference. We are dedicated to unlocking potential, not only for the countries we work in but also for each of our team members. No matter where you’re from or who you are, if you’re passionate about the transformative power of progressive politics, we invite you to build a better future with us. Role Summary About the Geopolitics Team TBI’s Geopolitics Team provides senior political and corporate leaders with distinctive, decision-relevant insight on the geopolitical forces shaping their priorities. The team briefs senior TBI leadership, government principals and C-suite clients, connecting political developments to their second- and third-order implications for strategy, policy, markets, investment, operations and risk. TBI is embedded with governments across the world and is growing its corporate client service footprint. The team therefore needs analysts who are equally comfortable briefing a senior public principal and a corporate executive, and who can translate complex political developments into clear implications for decisions. Role Overview The Senior Analyst will support TBI’s coverage of Asia-Pacific, with a particular focus on China. The successful candidate will bring strong foreign-policy judgement, regional expertise, analytical range and an established network across policy, diplomatic, business and expert communities. We are looking for someone who has the tools, curiosity and network to build informed views quickly across political, economic, security, trade, technology and market issues, and to turn fragmented information into distinctive insight for public and private clients. Candidates will need to have the existing right to work in the UK, as unfortunately we are unable to offer visa sponsorship for this role. Key Responsibilities Brief senior TBI leadership, public-sector principals and corporate clients on geopolitical developments across China and the wider Asia Pacific Region, with clear implications for decisions and risk exposure. Produce high-quality intelligence briefings, written analysis, data-led insights and client-ready deliverables on China and APAC. Identify second- and third-order implications of political, security, trade, sanctions, technology, election and foreign-policy developments for governments and businesses. Develop distinctive insights for corporate clients on how geopolitical risks affect strategy, supply chains, market exposure, investment decisions, regulation and operations. Draw on TBI’s internal capabilities and external expert networks to build robust perspectives, test assumptions and identify emerging risks and opportunities. Use quantitative and qualitative methods, including data visualisation, forecasting, scenario analysis, market data analysis, Excel and AI tools, to strengthen geopolitical analysis. Represent TBI in client briefings, workshops, conferences and external engagements, including through some travel. Support the growth of TBI’s geopolitics offer by helping shape new products, client propositions and analytical methods. Person Specification We are looking for an exceptional analyst with relevant experience in geopolitical risk, corporate intelligence, political advisory, foreign service, intelligence, consulting, government, think tanks or a similar environment. The successful candidate will have: Essential Strong relevant professional experience in a similar role or environment. Advanced degree in a relevant field, including Asian studies, international affairs, economics, political science or similar, or equivalent practical experience. Demonstrated expertise in Chinese and/or Asian geopolitics, evidenced through a publication record, prior roles, or equivalent body of work. Advanced proficiency in Mandarin, particularly reading, with the confidence to work directly with Chinese-language primary sources. The demonstrated ability to produce sharp, senior-facing intelligence briefings as confidently as they conduct quantitative analysis. Experience piecing together information from open sources, expert conversations, data, market indicators and institutional networks to generate original insight. Strong networks across foreign policy, diplomatic, business and expert communities relevant to the Americas. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to brief senior public principals and C-suite clients with clarity, judgement and confidence. Strong analytical capability across political risk, foreign policy, elections, trade and industrial policy, sanctions, technology, security and market impacts. Experience using data visualisation, forecasting, scenario analysis, market data and Excel to support analysis; Python would be a plus but is not required. An entrepreneurial, intellectually curious and self-starting approach, with the judgement to operate in ambiguous environments. Strong relationship-building skills and the ability to work across TBI to access internal and external expertise. Desirable Familiarity with AI tools and an interest in applying them responsibly to improve analytical quality and productivity. Exposure to client business development Additional areas of demonstrated thematic interest, including technology, trade, energy and security. Additional regional languages. Closing Date: 2026-08-30

Role Summary About the Geopolitics Team TBI’s Geopolitics Team provides senior political and corporate leaders with distinctive, decision-relevant insight on the geopolitical forces shaping their priorities. The team briefs senior TBI leadership, government principals and C-suite clients, connecting political developments to their second- and third-order implications for strategy, policy, markets, investment, operations and risk. TBI is embedded with governments across the world and is growing its corporate client service footprint. The team therefore needs analysts who are equally comfortable briefing a senior public principal and a corporate executive, and who can translate complex political developments into clear implications for decisions. Candidates will need to have the existing right to work in the UK, as unfortunately we are unable to offer visa sponsorship for this role. Role Overview The Senior Analyst will lead TBI’s coverage of the Americas, with a particular focus on the U.S. and Latin America, including Brazil, Argentina and Colombia. The successful candidate will bring strong foreign-policy judgement, regional expertise, analytical range and an established network across policy, diplomatic, business and expert communities. This is not a narrow country-specialist role. We are looking for someone who has the tools, curiosity and network to build informed views quickly across political, economic, security, trade, technology and market issues, and to turn fragmented information into distinctive insight for public and private clients. Candidates will need to have the existing right to work in the UK, as unfortunately we are unable to offer visa sponsorship for this role. Key Responsibilities Brief senior TBI leadership, public-sector principals and corporate clients on geopolitical developments across the Americas, with clear implications for decisions and risk exposure. Produce high-quality intelligence briefings, written analysis, data-led insights and client-ready deliverables on the U.S., Latin America and wider Americas dynamics. Identify second- and third-order implications of political, security, trade, sanctions, technology, election and foreign-policy developments for governments and businesses. Develop distinctive insights for corporate clients on how geopolitical risks affect strategy, supply chains, market exposure, investment decisions, regulation and operations. Draw on TBI’s internal capabilities and external expert networks to build robust perspectives, test assumptions and identify emerging risks and opportunities. Use quantitative and qualitative methods, including data visualisation, forecasting, scenario analysis, market data analysis, Excel and AI tools, to strengthen geopolitical analysis. Represent TBI in client briefings, workshops, conferences and external engagements, including through some travel. Support the growth of TBI’s geopolitics offer by helping shape new products, client propositions and analytical methods. Person Specification We are looking for an exceptional analyst with relevant experience in geopolitical risk, corporate intelligence, political advisory, foreign service, intelligence, consulting, government, think tanks or a similar environment. The successful candidate will have: Essential Strong relevant professional experience in a similar role or environment. Advanced degree in a relevant field, including international affairs, economics, political science or similar, or equivalent practical experience. Strong expertise in the Americas, with a clear spike in U.S. foreign policy and strong working knowledge of political and economic dynamics in Latin America. The demonstrated ability to produce sharp, senior-facing intelligence briefings as confidently as they conduct quantitative analysis. Experience piecing together information from open sources, expert conversations, data, market indicators and institutional networks to generate original insight. Strong networks across foreign policy, diplomatic, business and expert communities relevant to the Americas. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to brief senior public principals and C-suite clients with clarity, judgement and confidence. Strong analytical capability across political risk, foreign policy, elections, trade and industrial policy, sanctions, technology, security and market impacts. Experience using data visualisation, forecasting, scenario analysis, market data and Excel to support analysis; Python would be a plus but is not required. An entrepreneurial, intellectually curious and self-starting approach, with the judgement to operate in ambiguous environments. Strong relationship-building skills and the ability to work across TBI to access internal and external expertise. Desirable Familiarity with AI tools and an interest in applying them responsibly to improve analytical quality and productivity. Exposure to client business development Additional areas of demonstrated thematic interest, including technology, trade, energy and security. Fluency in Spanish and/or Portuguese is highly desirable. Closing Date: 2026-08-30

The postholder will deliver excellent logistical, operational and administrative support to our people and work closely with our teams on the ground. Core tasks Lead all aspects of the management and maintenance of TBI managed properties in Dubai. Support visa and work permit applications for staff in DIFC, and all related administrative processes for employment. HR and staffing: liase with central HR teams to manage onboarding of new staff, advise country staff on HR and staffing policies, support team members in country with ongoing work permit/visa queries. Admin: support the Managing Director and country leadership team with logistics support Travel: Ensure the consistent use of and adherence to the TBI travel management system and procedures Coordinate in country moves outside of core locations Support visa applications and arrival procedures of international staff and visitors to the programme Ensure that all international staff and visitors have a working means of communication within 24 hours of arrival in country Office operations Onboard and oversee local vendors including cleaners, local IT etc. Ensure the UAE government and company policies are being followed regarding protocols and procedures Liase with the Global Security and Operations Team to ensure protocols are followed and identify and flag operational risks to the Country Head Support projects with leadership visits and events as needed in the region with the logistics coordination between the teams involved Participate in the crisis management team in the event of a medical or security emergency. Finance Manage financial activities in compliance with TBI policy and procedures Support the Country Head and team in central financial management including preparing requests for advance of funds and/or direct payments; monitoring budget expenditures and maintaining a proper record of budgets and spending Safety, security and access With support from the Global Operations and Security team, develop country level security SOPs that are contextually appropriate to the risk to TBI staff and activities in country Maintain an active network with other agencies as well as key interlocutors to ensure that TBI understands the security context. Notify the Managing Director, Global Security and Operations Team when the political or security situation may impact TBI’s staff or activities Ensure that any violation of safety and security rules as well as security incidents are reported to the Managing Director and Global Operations and Security team Work with the Managing Director to enable safe access for TBI staff to new areas and identify key stakeholders and interlocutors relevant to the area of operation Ensure that all TBI locations are compliant with fire regulations and equipped with firefighting equipment where necessary Act as the point of contact in country to carry our security tasks as directed by the Global Security and Operations team Maintain an up to date country Flap sheet and communications tree. These duties will be communicated in advance and agreed with the Country Head where possible. Person Specification The individual should work to the highest standard with a keen attention to detail delivering workable solutions to various teams with competing priorities. They should proactively enagage with the business and be bold in their approach, working to make change for the better and improve operational efficiency and reduce the threat to our people, assets and reputation. They should be an ambassador for the team and build trust with those with whom they engage. They should be solution orientated. In addition, the postholder should be able to demonstrate more than three years’ of experience of: Programme management Security, operations, logistics and administration. Fluency in written and verbal English is required. Closing Date: 2026-08-24
